question: Should OpenClaw expose a rule-based host filesystem policy in core, and what canonical `tools.fs` API plus exec scope should be accepted?
rationale: The request defines a public config surface and security enforcement boundary, and the live related PRs show competing API shapes with unresolved exec coverage and upgrade semantics.

options.title: Settle one `tools.fs` contract
options.body: Choose a canonical allow/deny or roots model with deny precedence, normalization/symlink behavior, explicit exec scope, docs, and upgrade tests before landing implementation.

options.title: Land file-tool policy and split exec
options.body: Accept a file-tool-only first version only if shell-mediated access is clearly documented and a linked exec policy issue remains open.

options.title: Defer to OS/container isolation
options.body: Decline host path ACL config if maintainers want core to rely on OS permissions, sandbox backends, `workspaceOnly`, and plugin hooks only.

recommendation.title: Settle one `tools.fs` contract
recommendation.body: Choose a canonical allow/deny or roots model with deny precedence, normalization/symlink behavior, explicit exec scope, docs, and upgrade tests before landing implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest current history and prior-review signal on the existing workspace-only filesystem boundary.
